package_info.package_versions: prior to 2.4.8-0ubuntu2.1 (patched June 2024), specifically Ubuntu 24.04 LTS default
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a logic flaw in the handling of UNIX domain socket permissions, allowing an attacker to escalate privileges by exploiting a sequence of configuration changes and symlink attacks, ultimately leading to arbitrary root code execution. The vulnerability is not due to intentionally malicious code, but the resulting behavior enables privilege escalation and arbitrary command execution as root.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when cupsd is restarted via the ServerSetSettings DBus method, the Listen parameter is set to a symlink under attacker control, causing cupsd to perform a chmod 777 on the symlink target (/etc/cups/cupsd.conf), resulting in the configuration file becoming world-writable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing a privileged configuration file to be world-writable via a symlink is a classic privilege escalation technique that allows unprivileged users to gain write access to sensitive files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal configuration changes should not allow a non-root user to make privileged files world-writable or manipulate symlinks to escalate privileges. The Listen directive should only affect socket paths, not file permissions of unrelated files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Listen directives are used to configure socket paths for cupsd, but not to escalate privileges or change file permissions on configuration files.
key_indicators: Symlink from unprivileged location to privileged file
DBus ServerSetSettings call with Listen parameter pointing to symlink

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after gaining write access to cupsd.conf, the attacker adds a Listen directive pointing to a symlink to /etc/cups/cups-files.conf. On the next restart, cupsd performs chmod 777 on /etc/cups/cups-files.conf, making it world-writable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chaining symlink attacks to escalate from one privileged file to another is a hallmark of privilege escalation exploits, allowing the attacker to gain control over additional sensitive configuration files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Configuration files should not be writable by unprivileged users, nor should configuration changes allow arbitrary file permission changes on unrelated files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Listen directives are for socket configuration, not for manipulating unrelated file permissions or escalating privileges.
key_indicators: Chained symlink attack from one config file to another
DBus ServerSetSettings call with Listen parameter pointing to symlink

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after /etc/cups/cups-files.conf is made world-writable, the attacker sets the Group parameter in cups-files.conf to 'netdev', causing all external programs executed by cupsd (such as print filters) to run with group netdev privileges.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing the group for external program execution to a group with elevated privileges (netdev) is a privilege escalation step, as it allows the attacker to run code with access to sensitive system resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal users should not be able to change the execution group for privileged daemons or their child processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Changing the group may be legitimate for system administrators configuring print services, but not for unprivileged users or in the context of chained privilege escalation.
key_indicators: Modification of execution context for privileged processes
Group parameter in cups-files.conf set to netdev
Escalation to a group with special DBus or network permissions

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a print job is submitted to the attacker-controlled printer, the FoomaticRIPCommandLine in the PPD file executes an attacker-supplied Python script as the group netdev.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing the print filter command line to execute arbitrary code is a classic code injection technique, enabling the attacker to run custom scripts with elevated privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PPD files should not allow unprivileged users to execute arbitrary code as privileged groups, and print filters should only execute trusted binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom print filters may be used by administrators for advanced printing needs, but not for arbitrary code execution from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: PPD file with FoomaticRIPCommandLine executing non-standard script
Arbitrary command execution via print job
Execution of attacker-controlled script as group netdev

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when print job is processed by cups)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import dbus
bus = dbus.SystemBus()
wpasup = bus.get_object('fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1', '/fi/w1/wpa_supplicant1')
wpasup.CreateInterface({'ConfigFile': '/tmp/stage/wpa.conf'})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker-supplied Python script is executed as group netdev, and it calls the wpa_supplicant's CreateInterface DBus method, passing a configuration file that references an attacker-controlled shared object, resulting in wpa_supplicant (running as root) loading and executing attacker code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing DBus interfaces to trigger privileged daemons to load attacker-controlled code is a sophisticated privilege escalation technique, bridging the gap from group netdev to root.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal print jobs should not interact with network configuration daemons or cause privileged services to load arbitrary shared objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be network configuration by system tools, not by print jobs or unprivileged scripts.
key_indicators: DBus call to privileged service (fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1) from print filter
CreateInterface method invoked with attacker-controlled config
Loading of attacker-controlled configuration by wpa_supplicant

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
opensc_engine_path=/tmp/stage/libpayload.so
# libpayload.so contains a constructor that sets /usr/bin/python3 to setuid root
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when wpa_supplicant loads the attacker-supplied configuration, it loads the attacker-supplied shared object, which executes code as root (e.g., sets /usr/bin/python3 to setuid root), resulting in persistent root shell access for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading arbitrary shared objects from untrusted locations is a critical security flaw, especially when the code runs as root, as it enables full system compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: wpa_supplicant should only load trusted, system-provided shared objects, and should never execute code from world-writable or user-controlled locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate plugins or extensions may be loaded by wpa_supplicant, but only from trusted, system directories and never from /tmp or user-writable paths.
key_indicators: Arbitrary shared object loading from /tmp or user-writable path
Privilege escalation to root via shared object constructor
Modification of system binaries to setuid root

attack_chain.action: Create symlink from /tmp/stage/cupsd.conf to /etc/cups/cupsd.conf and use DBus ServerSetSettings to set Listen to this path.
Modify /etc/cups/cupsd.conf to add Listen /tmp/stage/cups-files.conf (symlink to /etc/cups/cups-files.conf), then trigger another ServerSetSettings call.
Set Group netdev in /etc/cups/cups-files.conf to ensure external programs run as group netdev.
attack_chain.leads_to: Print filters run as group netdev

attack_chain.action: Install a printer with a PPD file containing a FoomaticRIPCommandLine that executes an attacker-controlled Python script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution as group netdev

attack_chain.action: Submit a print job to trigger the Python script, which calls wpa_supplicant's CreateInterface method with a config referencing an attacker-controlled shared object.
attack_chain.leads_to: wpa_supplicant loads attacker-controlled shared object as root

attack_chain.action: wpa_supplicant loads the shared object, which sets /usr/bin/python3 to setuid root, enabling root shell access.

behavioral_signatures: Repeated DBus calls to org.opensuse.cupspkhelper ServerSetSettings with Listen parameters pointing to symlinks or non-standard paths
Unexpected changes to Group parameter in cups-files.conf (especially to netdev)
Installation of printers with PPD files containing FoomaticRIPCommandLine executing non-standard binaries or scripts
Print jobs triggering execution of scripts or binaries outside standard print filters
DBus calls to wpa_supplicant's CreateInterface from non-network management processes (e.g., print filters)
wpa_supplicant loading shared objects from non-standard paths (e.g., /tmp, /home, /var/tmp)
file_indicators: PPD files with FoomaticRIPCommandLine referencing /tmp or user-writable locations
network_indicators: DBus traffic to org.opensuse.cupspkhelper and fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 from non-standard clients (e.g., print filters or user scripts)
Unusual DBus method calls (ServerSetSettings, PrinterAddWithPpdFile, CreateInterface) from user sessions or non-root processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DBus calls to org.opensuse.cupspkhelper with Listen parameters pointing to symlinks or non-standard paths, and for repeated changes to cups configuration files' permissions. Alert on world-writable permissions set on /etc/cups/cupsd.conf or /etc/cups/cups-files.conf. Flag any PPD files with FoomaticRIPCommandLine executing scripts or binaries outside standard print filters. Monitor wpa_supplicant for attempts to load shared objects from non-system directories (e.g., /tmp, /home). Correlate print job submissions with subsequent DBus calls to wpa_supplicant and changes to setuid binaries (e.g., /usr/bin/python3).
